key_insight: GenAI advice scored higher than primary care physicians’ advice in six of seven evaluated dimensions, but not readability.
clinical_relevance: GenAI may support structured chronic disease self-management advice, but this study does not establish benefits for patients in clinical practice.
method: Source-blinded comparison using 15 diabetes and hypertension vignettes across three simulated management stages.
One GenAI system and 22 primary care physicians independently generated advice.
Three clinician raters assessed seven dimensions; comparisons used linear mixed-effects models and robustness analyses.
evidence_signal: GenAI’s adjusted score advantage was 1.16–1.56 points across six dimensions (P<.001), while readability showed no significant difference (−0.22; 95% CI −0.54 to 0.11).
watch_item: Vignette-based clinician ratings of one GenAI system do not establish real-world safety, patient understanding, or long-term outcomes.
paper_title: Generative AI Versus Primary Care Physicians from Plan Initiation to Long-Term Maintenance of Chronic Disease Self-Management: A Vignette-Based Validation Study
